newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BAESA says hit bottom, headed for recovery.
newsitem.headline: BAESA says hit bottom, headed for recovery.

text.p: The president of Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), which has just announced it lost $452 million in the year to Sept 30, said it has hit bottom and is headed for recovery.

"We don't want to sound victorious, but recovery signs are clear," BAESA President and CEO Luis Suarez said in an interview with the newspaper La Nacion. "We already hit bottom and are starting to go up."

Among other achievements, during that period cash flow went from negative to positive in October, costs were trimmed, marginal contribution per case showed a dramatic improvement, and a new management team took charge in Brazil, which "was the biggest" problem, Suarez told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange when the results were announced earlier this week.
"Now that the 100-day plan has been completed, I think the greatest part of the restructuring effort is over," he said earlier this week.
Also in October BAESA reached a standstill agreement with its leading creditors to defer until March 31 repayments of capital of about $520 million in debts.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires Metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
In September shareholders of BAESA filed a class action suit in Manhattan federal court against both BAESA and PEPSI alleging they hid the bottler's problems.
BAESA, the biggest Pepsi Co bottler outside the United States, said this week its loss in the year compared to a $44.8 million gain in the 1995 fiscal year.
But Suarez said the last results should be seen as "house cleaning", adding that "now we will be in better shape, we are strenghtened."
In July Pepsi took over operating control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion. Since then the new management launched a 100-day recovery plan.
-- Guillermo Hskel, Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
